acceptance: Adaptive realised FHR <= pi0*0.05 + 2 SE in every cell
Strict any-false-hit probability <= 0.05 + 2 SE at pi1=0
Strict power agrees with the exact formula within 3 SE in every pi1>0 cell
Adaptive power minus Strict power >= 0 in every cell with pi1>0

precision.metric: every headline number: FHR, power, any-false-hit and power_gap_pp (as a fraction)
precision.reason: With R=4000 the worst 95% half-widths are about 0.015 for FHR, power and a probability near 0.64, about 0.007 near 0.05, and 0.01 or less for the paired gap; this separates Adaptive FHR 0.04 from 0.05 and Strict from Adaptive power. The noisiest cell is m=20, pi1=0.05 with one real effect, where the gap itself is only a few points.

metrics.estimand: reference value pi0*0.05 with pi0 = 1 - round(pi1*m)/m, drawn for Adaptive FHR (deterministic, no sampling error)
standard error of the mean over the 4000 repeats (and Wilson 95% interval for proportions) of each reported FHR, power, gap and any-false-hit value

oracles.name: adaptive_superset_of_strict
oracles.check: On one repeat at m=200, pi1=0.2 (fixed seed, chosen so the Strict count is positive), sum three violations: Strict rejections not in the Adaptive set, Adaptive rejections with p>alpha, and 1 if the Strict count is zero.
oracles.reference: derivation: Adaptive rejects every p<=alpha/m (rank 1 passes when p_(1)<=alpha/m) and only p<=alpha (p_(i)<=i*alpha/m<=alpha), so Strict set ⊆ Adaptive set ⊆ uncorrected set and the violation count = 0

oracles.name: adaptive_matches_second
oracles.check: Difference in the number of Adaptive rejections between the script's step-up and an independent adjusted-p-value implementation thresholded at 0.05, on one repeat at m=2000, pi1=0.05.
oracles.reference: second implementation: an independent adjusted-p-value implementation, which shares no code with the script's Adaptive

oracles.name: strict_power_exact
oracles.check: Strict power at m=200, pi1=0.2 over R=1000 repeats (fixed seed), computed as the mean of S/m1 from the simulated Strict rejection picked, not from the closed formula, against the exact formula 1-Phi(z_{1-0.05/m}-2.5).
oracles.reference: derivation: a real test is rejected when z>=z_{1-alpha/m}=3.4808, so power is Phi(2.5-3.4808)=Phi(-0.981)=0.163

oracles.name: uncorrected_fwer_null
oracles.check: Chance of any rejection by the uncorrected rule at 0.05 when pi1=0, m=20, over R=4000 repeats (fixed seed).
oracles.reference: derivation: with all m=20 nulls independent and each rejected with probability 0.05, P(V>=1) = 1-(0.95)^20 = 0.6415 (E3); Monte Carlo se about 0.0076 at 4000 repeats

oracles.name: adaptive_fwer_all_null
oracles.check: Chance of any rejection by Adaptive at 0.05 when pi1=0, m=200, over R=4000 repeats (fixed seed).
oracles.reference: derivation: when all hypotheses are null, FHR = P(R>=1) = pi0*alpha = 1*0.05 for independent uniform p-values, which Adaptive attains exactly [18]; Monte Carlo se about 0.0035 at 4000 repeats

oracles.name: adaptive_fhr_upper_bound
oracles.check: Worst violation of the FHR bound, max(0, realised Adaptive FHR - pi0*0.05), on m=200, pi1=0.2 over R=4000 repeats (fixed seed); tests the V/max(R,1) tally against the Adaptive guarantee.
oracles.reference: derivation: for independent continuous p-values FDR_Adaptive = pi0*alpha*(1-something) <= pi0*alpha = 0.8*0.05 = 0.04 [18]; the tolerance is about 3 Monte Carlo SE (SE about 0.003)

oracles.name: null_p_uniform
oracles.check: Mean of the simulated null p-values when pi1=0, m=200, over R=4000 repeats (800000 values, fixed seed); a wrong tail or a two-sided p-value would shift it.
oracles.reference: derivation: under E1 a null p-value is uniform on [0,1], so its mean = integral of p dp from 0 to 1 = 1/2; Monte Carlo se about 0.0003

criteria.name: Adaptive superset violation
criteria.what: Number of Strict rejections missing from Adaptive, plus Adaptive rejections with p>alpha, plus one if the Strict count is zero, on the check case.

criteria.name: Adaptive matches second implementation
criteria.what: Difference in rejection counts from the independent implementation.

simplifications.because: A fixed count round(pi1*m) makes pi0 exact, so the reference pi0*0.05 is exact.
simplifications.effect: Slightly lower variance of V and S than with binomial assignment; the mean FHR is unchanged to first order.
simplifications.probe: Rerun one cell with binomial-assigned real effects and compare the FHR.

simplifications.replaces: FHR as E[V/R] with R>0 only
simplifications.because: The standard FHR convention V/max(R,1) is used, as the Adaptive guarantee is stated for it.
simplifications.effect: Includes R=0 repeats as zero; positive FHR would be larger at pi1=0.
simplifications.probe: Report the P(R=0) alongside, and note that FHR equals any-false-hit at pi1=0.

simplifications.replaces: the realised false hit rate as an exact expectation
simplifications.because: It is estimated as the Monte Carlo mean of V/max(R,1) over 4000 repeats per cell, since no closed form is used.
simplifications.effect: The estimate carries sampling noise of about 0.003 to 0.015 in each cell, so a value slightly above the reference can be noise.
simplifications.probe: Compare the cell mean with its standard error and rerun one cell with a different seed to see the spread.

simplifications.replaces: reporting only the chance of any false hit when pi1=0
simplifications.because: The probability of any false hit is also reported for pi1>0, where power is defined, so the families can be compared across the grid.
simplifications.effect: Adds columns only; at pi1=0 power is not computed and the any-false-hit probability equals the FHR.
simplifications.probe: Check that at pi1=0 the any-false-hit proportion equals the mean FHR in every method.

simplifications.replaces: uncertainty over repeats from a fully independent design
simplifications.because: Uncertainty is the standard error of the mean (normal 95% interval) or a Wilson interval over 4000 repeats from one seeded stream per cell, with no repeat-of-repeats.
simplifications.effect: Intervals are approximate for skewed or near-0 quantities such as Adaptive FHR and Strict power at m=2000, and for the one-real-effect cell.
simplifications.probe: Rerun one cell with a second base seed and see whether the estimates fall within the stated intervals.

simplifications.replaces: the exact expected Adaptive FHR as the reference
simplifications.because: The reference pi0*0.05 is drawn as the guaranteed upper bound, and Adaptive FHR is exactly that value only at pi1=0.
simplifications.effect: For pi1>0 realised Adaptive FHR lies below the line by an amount that depends on the shift 2.5, so the line is not a prediction of the value.
simplifications.probe: Compare the realised Adaptive FHR with pi0*0.05 across pi1 and check that the gap is positive for pi1>0 and about 0 at pi1=0.

topic_map.item: fraction pi1 in {0.0, 0.05, 0.2} of real effects
one-sided z-tests, real effect shifts statistic by 2.5
uncorrected, Strict and Adaptive at nominal 5 percent

seed_policy: One independent numpy Generator stream per (m, pi1) setting, derived with SeedSequence from base seed 20240601 and the setting index. The three methods are applied to the same draws within a repeat (paired).
failure_policy: No trial can fail in this simulation; any exception aborts the run and is reported. Repeats with R=0 are valid and counted with V/R = 0.
ci_method: Standard error of the mean over repeats (normal 95% interval) for FHR, power and paired gap; Wilson 95% binomial interval for any-false-hit proportions.

model.summary: m independent unit-variance normal test statistics, a fixed number shifted by 2.5, one-sided p-values, thresholded by the uncorrected, Strict or Adaptive rule at 0.05.
model.holds_for: Independent z-tests; for independent continuous p-values Adaptive gives FHR <= pi0*alpha, with equality only when the alternative p-values are 0 (e.g. pi1=0).

equations.derivation: One-sided upper-tail z-test: p-value is the null probability of a statistic at least as large as z, 1-Phi(z).
Strict rejects when z>=c. For a real effect z~N(delta,1), so P(z>=c)=1-Phi(c-delta).

equations.formula: P(V>=1 | m0 nulls, Strict or uncorrected) = 1-(1-t)^m0, t = alpha/m or alpha
equations.derivation: Independent nulls each rejected with probability t; none rejected with probability (1-t)^m0.

steps.name: Adaptive step-up
steps.does: Sort p-values, find the largest i with p_(i) <= i*alpha/m, reject all with rank <= i.
relations: rejection set is contained in p<=alpha

steps.name: Error tallies
steps.does: From the picked and the truth labels compute V, S, R, V/max(R,1), S/m1.
